findings: The authoritative library function has six top-level statements: ActionProcess guard, explicit cardID lookup, notifier call, return/end. Its notification field contexts read only the lookup object; no receiver/self fallback exists.

Public object convenience calls now convert the argument to its ID and resolve the current map before serializing names/JSON. Dispatcher object aliases and integer arguments use the same path; internal Pincer persistence shares it.

A missing or nonpositive target no longer causes dispatcher fallback to serialize the caller. Existing headless skipping of invalid-object notifications is retained as an unresolved model boundary, not certified as the native result.

24 identity cases exercise both sides, public/dispatcher integer/dispatcher alias routes, detached aliases and same-ID replacements, both refresh flag values.36 invalid-input scenarios reject caller identity/payload leakage and synthetic nonpositive map fields without asserting native missing notification count.

Read-only Ghidra exports match installed EXE bytes for the JSON conversion wrapper/body, frame step and common object-context handler. The conversion body zeroes the output FString then serializes only when the input shared object is nonnull: invalid BlueprintJson serializes to empty string.

The EX_Context0x19 static initializer installs RVA15a3550 at GNativeFuncs+19*8; its thunk jumps to159bfa0. The null-context path skips the expression and uses property clearing/initialization. Exact BlueprintJson struct default construction after that virtual call remains unresolved, so no missing notification payload is guessed.
limits: This fixes notification object identity and excludes caller fallback. It does not complete invalid-object emission/default payloads or the full persistence receiver/network lifecycle.

NotifyPersistCustomFields, HandlePersistCustomFields and the OnlineMatch notifier path use parsed pak authority; these functions are absent from the saved runtime bytecode capture. Three lookup/library functions have runtime identity and branch checks.

Ghidra native export proves bytes and the observed invalid-shared-object serialization branch; struct property ClearValue/CppStructOps defaults and every UObject access-none/error state are not proven.
The same-named JSON registration getter/thunk was located statically; broader native symbol/type ownership and all serializer formatting/number behavior remain outside this bounded audit.

Object aliases, mapping replacement, omitted/null parameters and invalid IDs are controlled fixtures, not proof real PvP cards necessarily produce them. The invalid-case test intentionally avoids asserting native notification count/default payload.
ActionProcess=false, pending-kill/GC, refresh/UI receiver semantics, queue and native ABI remain open. UI work is excluded from the headless simulator scope.

No KARDS process was running at the check; work used authoritative saved captures/pak and installed EXE plus the supplied Ghidra project in read-only/noanalysis mode. No client memory writes, injection or historical replay authority. Fully semantically verified cards remains0.
